diffs.reason: FSL-117, corrected by default with a notice: with membrane energy, Levenberg-Marquardt's Hessian of the regularisation divides each derivative by the voxel size in mm while the cost and its gradient count in voxels; the default takes the Hessian in the cost's units, so the steps follow the cost they minimise (the final cost is never higher: −0.00 to −1.66 % on the measured cases). `reproduce` gives FSL's bytes. FSL-201, corrected by default with a notice (since 2026-11-03): with the movements estimated, FSL's derivatives of the cost with respect to the rotations are forward differences (steps of 10⁻⁵ rad) of rotation matrices built from a single-precision angle, cosine and sine, so the rounding divided by the step makes its gradient and its Gauss-Newton Hessian of the movements other than the cost's (their rotation entries 0.25 to 39 % off on ds005040's pair at half resolution) and the minimisers end elsewhere than the cost's minimum; the default computes the exact derivatives. Measured on 22 runs that estimate the movements, the default's final cost was lower or equal in 18 (the other four, runs cut short, 0.004 to 0.13 % higher), lower in all 8 random cases whose volumes moved (by 0.01 to 44 %), and 38 % lower after 60 iterations of scaled conjugate gradients on the half-resolution pair, where FSL's stall; fMRIPrep's calls estimate no movements and stay the same. `reproduce` gives FSL's bytes.

examples.title: applytopup --method=vb3D, and a correction by default
examples.summary: The record's case `at/vb3d-y`: one of applytopup's undocumented variational Bayes restorations (a smoothness prior within and between slices, its weights estimated over 20 iterations). FSL 6.0.7.23 and the replica's `reproduce` give the same bytes, and both diverge: the prior FSL builds couples the slices with half its weight, which makes it indefinite (FSL-143). The replica's default gives the prior its full weight (and resamples the first image with the spline interpolation asked for, FSL-132): its restoration stays in the input's range. Choose *each image's own* window to read FSL's output. LARMORX's clean room runs the same call in `reproduce` (at 14 threads and at one) and in `fix`, its default, which corrects FSL-143.
